citations.quote: I have had three sinus infections since June, and my GP thinks the bedroom is the reason.
In the bedroom the paint behind the wardrobe is coming off in patches and there are black spots spreading up to the ceiling; the room has smelled of a damp cellar since the spring.
Since mid-September the heating fails every few days and the flat cools to about 15 degrees until someone restarts it.
I'm planning to put my October rent into the official deposit account rather than pay it to them, and to keep doing that until the heating is fixed and the bedroom wall is dealt with.

plan.because: Needed to establish the parties, property and tenancy terms.
Obtain the two emails to establish what defects were reported and when.
Establish whether and when the landlord received the reports.
Document the affected location, visible condition and dates.
Establish the response, any proposed work and access arrangements.
The reported damp bedroom and black spots activate the moisture branch.
Heating failures are reported; obtain any inspection and service findings.
Health effects are reported; obtain findings and any limits on the attributed cause.
A need for specialist inspection is not mentioned, so it is presumed absent for planning; the cause remains open.
A rent deposit is contemplated; establish whether a repair deadline was communicated and its contents before assessing safeguards.

questions: Is the flat currently safe and adequately heated, and is anyone experiencing urgent symptoms? Seek appropriate urgent help if needed.
When were the two emails sent, what did they report, and is there proof the landlord received them?
Has any written repair deadline already been sent? Please provide it if so; obtain advice on the safeguards before depositing rent.
Have heating service findings, dated photographs, or medical confirmation already been obtained?
